lessonText.ser-vs-estar: Ser vs estar Ser vs estar Portuguese has two verbs for “to be”. Choosing the right one is one of the first big hurdles — but the patterns repeat. Identity and traits with ser; location, mood, and ongoing action with estar. A1 ser-vs-estar Quick rule Ser Estar Identity, nationality, profession Location (where someone is now) Defining traits (often long-lasting) Temporary feelings and moods What something is (type, quality in general) Changeable state — how things are right now “Permanent vs temporary” is a useful shortcut, but meaning and context matter more — see below. Ser — who / what / when Use ser for identity, origin, profession, and traits you present as part of who someone is — not where they happen to be at the moment. Ele é arquiteto. · Nós somos portugueses. · Eu sou professora. He is an architect. · We are Portuguese. · I am a teacher. Eu sou loira. · Ele é de Lisboa. · São três horas. I am blond. · He is from Lisbon. · It is three o'clock. O café é caro, mas é bom. The coffee is expensive, but it is good. (general quality) Personality and character often take ser when you mean a general trait: Eu sou ansioso. I am an anxious person. (usually / by nature) Estar — where / how (now) Use estar for location, health, mood, hunger, and situations that can change — even if they last a while. Estou em casa. · Ele está na cozinha. · Ela está cansada. I am at home. · He is in the kitchen. · She is tired. O café está quente. · Nós estamos com fome. · Eu estou desempregado. The coffee is hot. (right now) · We are hungry. · I am unemployed. (current situation) Como estás? — Estou bem, obrigada. How are you? — I am fine, thanks. The same adjective with estar often means a passing feeling: Eu estou ansioso. I am feeling anxious. (right now) Same adjective, different meaning Some adjectives change meaning depending on the verb: With ser With estar é ansioso — he is an anxious person está ansioso — he is feeling anxious now é mau — he is a bad person está mau — he is unwell é verde — it is green (colour) está verde — it is unripe é seguro — it is safe (in general) está seguro — he feels safe Common mistakes Do not use ser for where someone is: Estou em Lisboa , not *Sou em Lisboa . Do not use estar for nationality or profession: Sou português , not *Estou português . English “to be” does not always map to the same verb — check whether you mean identity/type or current state. With adjectives, sou vs estou can change the meaning entirely ( sou ansioso vs estou ansioso ). Progressive actions Ongoing actions use estar + a + infinitive in European Portuguese (not gerund like Brazilian PT): Estou a estudar português. · Eles estão a jantar. I am studying Portuguese. · They are having dinner. Memory hook: Ser = essence (who/what). Estar = state (where/how now). Location almost always takes estar : Lisboa é bonita (in general) but Estou em Lisboa (I am there now). Conjugation Ser is irregular in every tense; estar is regular in the present (and still worth learning in other tenses). In speech you may hear shortened forms like tá for está — fine in conversation, not in formal writing. Practise on the verb list: look up ser and estar . Related: Present continuous (EP) · Adjectives
lessonText.articles-gender: Articles & gender Articles & gender Every noun in Portuguese is masculine or feminine. The article (o, a, os, as) must agree. Definite and indefinite articles, gender hints, and EP article habits. A1 articles-gender Definite articles Singular Plural Masculine o livro os livros Feminine a casa as casas Indefinite articles Singular Plural Masculine um livro uns livros Feminine uma casa umas casas Guessing gender from the ending Often feminine : ends in -a ( a mesa , a porta ) Often masculine : ends in -o ( o gato , o carro ) Also common: -ção → feminine ( a nação ); -or → often masculine ( o professor ) Endings are hints, not rules. O dia , a mão , o problema break the pattern — learn gender with the word. When EP uses the definite article European Portuguese uses o/a more often than English uses “the”: Gosto do café. · A Maria telefonou. · Vou para a escola. I like coffee. · Maria called. · I am going to school. Before names in familiar speech: a Ana , o João With many country names: o Canadá , o Brasil After gostar de , the noun often keeps its article: gosto do cinema When you often skip the article Sou professora. · Ele é médico. I'm a teacher. · He's a doctor. — no article with professions after ser. Contractions (very common) Prepositions merge with articles: de + article em + article a + article do, da, dos, das no, na, nos, nas ao, à, aos, às Venho da escola. · Estou no café. · Vou ao mercado. I come from school. · I am at the café. · I am going to the market. When you learn a new noun, always learn it with its article: a mesa , not just mesa . Related: Plurals · Prepositions in depth · A1 vocabulary
lessonText.presente-regular: Present tense — regular verbs Present tense (regular) The present indicative (presente do indicativo) describes habits, facts, and actions happening now. This is what the verb conjugations page shows for hundreds of common A1–B2 verbs. -ar / -er / -ir endings, stem changes, and what the present can mean. A1 presente-regular Three conjugation groups -ar verbs — falar , trabalhar , estudar -er verbs — comer , beber , vender -ir verbs — partir , abrir , decidir Person endings (-ar example: falar) Person Ending Example eu -o falo tu -as falas ele / ela / você -a fala nós -amos falamos vocês / eles / elas -am falam In European Portuguese, tu is common in speech; você is more formal. -er example: comer eu como nós comemos tu comes vocês comem ele/ela come eles/elas comem -ir example: partir eu parto nós partimos tu partes vocês partem ele/ela parte eles/elas partem Some -ir verbs use -e- in the present ( decidir → decido ) while others stay regular ( partir → parto ). The verb list shows the actual forms. Stem changes (still “regular” in textbooks) Many verbs tweak the vowel in the stem for eu, tu, ele, eles but keep the same endings: poder → posso, podes, pode · comer → como · sentir → sinto, sentes, sente These are predictable once you know the pattern — check each verb on the list. Regular vs irregular — quick overview Regular verbs keep the same stem and take the -ar / -er / -ir endings above. Irregular verbs change the stem or use special forms (ser → sou, ir → vou, ter → tenho). Learn regular patterns first, then the high-frequency irregulars on the irregular-present and core-verbs pages. Rule of thumb If the dictionary lists a normal -ar/-er/-ir infinitive and no “irregular” note → use the endings on this page. Common irregulars to learn early: ser, estar, ir, ter, fazer, haver, dizer, dar, ver, saber, querer, poder . Stem-changing verbs (pedir → peço) are often still taught as “regular with a stem tweak” — endings stay the same. What the present can mean Habit: Trabalho em casa. — I work from home. Right now: Como sopa. — I am eating soup. Future (informal): Amanhã vou ao médico. — Tomorrow I am going to the doctor. lessonText.cognate-patterns: Cognate patterns Cognate patterns English and Portuguese share thousands of Latin-derived words. Ending patterns often match — which speeds up reading — but watch for spelling and gender shifts. -tion/-ção, -ty/-dade, and false friends to watch for. A1 cognate-patterns Patterns that often work English ending Portuguese Examples -tion -ção (f.) information → a informação -ity -idade (f.) university → a universidade -ous -oso / -osa famous → famoso, famosa -ly (adverb) -mente quickly → rapidamente -al -al national → nacional -ent / -ant -ente / -ante different → diferente Verb lookalikes (-ar verbs) English verbs in -ate often become Portuguese -ar: communicate → comunicar · participate → participar · organise → organizar Stress and vowels change, but recognition is instant. Same spelling, different part of speech Verb: Eles circulam pela cidade. · Adj.: Uma estrada circular. They move around the city. · A ring road. Spelling shifts to remember ph → f: phone → telefone ct → ct or just c: action → ação ss / s / ç: necessary → necessário Silent letters drop: psychology → psicologia False friends look related but mean something else — e.g. preservativo (condom), excitado (aroused, not “excited” in the English sense). Always check meaning, not just shape. Use cognates to guess at text, then confirm with context. Pair with False friends (EP) . Related: Articles & gender · A1 vocabulary
lessonText.ask-nicely: Asking nicely Asking nicely European Portuguese softens requests. Direct “I want…” is understood, but locals usually use the courtesy imperfect and a few set phrases. Queria, podia, será que, and faz favor for polite EP requests. A2 ask-nicely Core idea Use the imperfeito of querer, poder, precisar, gostar, preferir for polite requests — even though you are asking about now . Add por favor or se faz favor . Literal meaning is “I wanted / could…”; in context it means “I'd like / could you…”. Direct → polite Too blunt Natural EP Quero um café. Queria um café, por favor. Preciso de ajuda. Precisava de ajuda, se faz favor. Pode trazer água? Podia trazer mais um copo de água? Quero ver a ementa. Gostava de ver a ementa. Common courtesy forms Queria uma mesa para dois. · Preferia um quarto mais calmo. I'd like a table for two. · I'd prefer a quieter room. Podia falar consigo? · Precisava de uma fatura. Could I speak with you (formal)? · I'd need a receipt. Era para… Useful at counters and on the phone — “I'm here to…” / “I was hoping to…”: Era para marcar uma consulta. · Era para levantar uma encomenda. I was hoping to book an appointment. · I'm here to pick up a parcel. Será que…? Adds uncertainty — “I wonder if… / Would it be possible…?”: Será que me pode ajudar? · Será que dá para pagar com cartão? I wonder if you could help me? · Would it be possible to pay by card? Importa-se de…? / Importas-te de…? “Would you mind…?” — formal vs informal: Importa-se de repetir? · Importas-te de fechar a janela? Would you mind repeating? (formal) · Would you mind closing the window? (tu) Please Por favor — neutral, always safe Se faz favor — very common in cafés and shops Complaints: open with Desculpe / Lamento incomodar , hedge with parece que… / acho que… , then ask for a fix with podia… or será que… . Practise: querer , poder , gostar · Related: Conditional
lessonText.demonstratives: Demonstratives — isto, isso, este, esse… Demonstratives Portuguese points to things with distance (near speaker, near listener, far from both) and with either a noun (variable forms) or no noun (isto / isso / aquilo). Este/esse/aquele vs isto/isso/aquilo — distance and EP usage. A2 demonstratives Two groups Variable — este/essa/aquele… agree with the noun. Used before a noun or as pronouns. Invariable (neuter) — isto, isso, aquilo never change and never sit before a noun. Three distances Distance Variable (masc. sg.) Neuter pronoun Typical use Near the speaker este livro isto this · here · now Near the listener esse livro isso that · what you said Far from both aquele livro aquilo that over there Variable forms (with a noun) Masc. sg. Masc. pl. Fem. sg. Fem. pl. Near speaker este estes esta estas Near listener esse esses essa essas Far aquele aqueles aquela aquelas Este livro é meu. · Essa caneta é minha. · Isto é um absurdo. This book is mine. · That pen is mine. · This is absurd. Contractions (very common) Nisto não há problema. · Por isso não vim. · Nada disso! There's no problem with this. · That's why I didn't come. · No way! European Portuguese vs Brazilian In everyday EP, este/esta/isto are normal for “this” near the speaker. In much of Brazil, esse/essa/isso cover a wider range. EP: Passas-me estes dois vestidos, por favor? Could you hand me these two dresses? (near the speaker) Memory hook: Speaker = este/isto . Listener = esse/isso . Distant = aquele/aquilo . Related: Articles & gender · Possessives
lessonText.haver: Haver Haver Haver is irregular and appears constantly in European Portuguese — most often as impersonal há (“there is / there are”), but also in compound tenses and set phrases. Impersonal há, time há dois anos, há de — not ter for existence. A2 haver What you hear every day Há — there is / there are · time passed (“há dois anos”) Há de — will probably ( eu hei de ir… ) Havia — there was / used to be With ter + havido — compound tenses Impersonal há — existence & time No subject pronoun: the verb is always third person. Há um café perto daqui. · Há muitas pessoas na rua. There is a café nearby. · There are many people on the street. Há muito tempo que não nos víamos. · Há quatro janelas na sala. It has been a long time since we saw each other. · There are four windows in the living room. Present indicative (personal forms) Form Note eu hei often hei de + infinitive tu hás ele/ela há also impersonal “there is” nós havemos vocês/eles hão rare; impersonal stays há Eu hei de ir amanhã. · Tu hás de gostar deste livro. I'll probably go tomorrow. · You're bound to like this book. Haver vs ter Ter = to have (ownership, age, hunger). Haver = existence / “there is”, time elapsed, and auxiliary in some compound forms. Do not use haver for “I have a car” → Tenho um carro. Há is not “have” in English. Há dois cafés = there are two cafés, not “I have two cafés”. Practise: haver · Also: ter · Related: Compound tenses
lessonText.core-verbs: Core Portuguese verbs Core verbs Start with a small set of high-frequency verbs — then learn patterns (-ar / -er / -ir) and irregular stems. Every verb below is in our conjugation table. ~22 essential verbs with links to the conjugation table. A1 core-verbs Three groups -ar — falar, gostar, precisar… -er — comer, querer, saber… -ir — partir, dormir… See Present tense — regular verbs . Ser & estar (to be) Verb English Practise ser to be (identity, type, origin) conjugation estar to be (location, mood, ongoing) conjugation Full guide: Ser vs estar . Top everyday verbs (irregular) Verb English Practise ter to have conjugation haver there is/are conjugation ir to go conjugation vir to come conjugation fazer to do / make conjugation poder can / to be able to conjugation querer to want conjugation saber to know (facts/how) conjugation dar to give conjugation dizer to say conjugation trazer to bring conjugation High-frequency regulars Verb English Practise falar to speak conjugation gostar (de) to like conjugation precisar (de) to need conjugation comer to eat conjugation beber to drink conjugation ficar to stay / become conjugation levar to take (away) conjugation ligar to call / turn on conjugation perguntar to ask conjugation vender to sell conjugation Quero um café, por favor. · Gosto muito de comida portuguesa. · Estou a estudar. I want a coffee, please. · I really like Portuguese food. · I am studying. lessonText.prepositions: Preposition pairings Preposition pairings Many Portuguese verbs and adjectives need a fixed preposition before their complement (regência). Learn the pairing with the word — don't translate prepositions one-by-one from English. Gostar de, pensar em, estar a, and a starter pairing table. A2 prepositions Classic starter gostar de — to like precisar de — to need estar a + infinitive — to be doing (EP continuous) Same verb, different preposition = different meaning falar falar com alguém — talk with someone · falar de algo — talk about something pensar pensar em — have on your mind · pensar de — have an opinion about Estou a pensar em ti. · O que pensas desta ideia? estar estar a ler — be reading · estar em casa — be at home · estar com fome — be hungry ir ir a — go to (visit) · ir para — go to (destination) · ir de — go by (transport) Vou ao supermercado. · Vou para casa. · Vou de comboio. High-frequency list (learn these first) Pairing English gostar de to like precisar de to need lembrar-se de to remember esquecer-se de to forget depender de to depend on ter de / ter que to have to começar a to start to aprender a to learn to concordar com to agree with interessar-se por to be interested in After de / em / a , articles often contract: gosto do café , estou na escola , vou ao médico . See articles & gender . Don't force English prepositions: “think about” is often pensar em , not pensar sobre for everyday “on my mind”. Related: Prepositions in depth · Por vs para · Verb list
lessonText.possessives: Possessives — meu or o meu? Possessives European Portuguese often puts a definite article before possessives: o meu livro. Sometimes the article drops. Both can be correct — the difference is emphasis and structure. O meu vs meu — EP article rules with possessives. A2 possessives Forms (agree with the thing owned) m. sg. f. sg. m. pl. f. pl. my meu minha meus minhas your (tu) teu tua teus tuas his / her / your (você) seu sua seus suas our nosso nossa nossos nossas your (vocês) vosso vossa vossos vossas Default EP pattern Before a noun: usually article + possessive — as minhas chaves , o nosso carro . Standing alone as “mine / yours”: usually no article — Os sapatos são meus . At the start of a sentence as pronoun: keep the article — O meu é azul . With article vs without — nuance Eles são meus filhos. · Eles são os meus filhos. They are my children. · THEY are my children. (emphasis) Esta casa é minha. · Esta casa é a minha. This house is mine. · THIS one is mine. Brazilian Portuguese drops the article more often. In EP, when in doubt with a noun, prefer o meu / a minha… . Seu / sua can mean his, her, their, or your (formal). Context (or dele / dela ) resolves ambiguity. Related: Articles & gender · Demonstratives
lessonText.plurals: Forming plurals Plurals Most Portuguese nouns and adjectives add -s or -es in the plural. A handful of patterns (-ões, irregular) cover most of what you'll meet at A1. -s, -es, -ões, and common irregular plurals. A1 plurals Default: add -s o livro → os livros · a casa → as casas · o gato → os gatos Ends in a vowel → add -s. Consonant endings: add -es o animal → os animais · o professor → os professores · a mulher → as mulheres -l often becomes -is; -r/-z/-n → -es. -ão → -ões / -ães / -ões Singular Plural a nação as nações o cão os cães o pão os pães Irregular / learn-with-the-word o mês → os meses · o país → os países · a mão → as mãos · o olho → os olhos Articles and adjectives must agree in number too: as casas bonitas , not *as casa bonita . Learn plural with the singular when you first meet a word — gender + plural together. Related: Articles & gender · Adjectives
lessonText.questions-negation: Questions & negation Questions & negation Portuguese questions often keep normal word order — intonation or a question word does the work. Negation is usually a single não before the verb, plus words like nunca and é que. Question words, não, nunca, and é que in EP. A1 questions-negation Yes/no questions Tu falas português? · Ele está em casa? · Queres café? Rising intonation; no “do” auxiliary like English. Question words Word Meaning Example o que / que what O que queres? quem who Quem é? onde where Onde ficas? quando when Quando chegas? como how Como te chamas? porque / porquê why Porque não vens? qual which Qual preferes? quanto how much Quanto custa? É que — EP flavour É que adds emphasis or softens a question. Very common in spoken EP: O que é que queres? · Onde é que ficas? · Porque é que não vens? What do you want? · Where do you live? · Why aren't you coming? Negation não before the verb: Não falo francês. Double negatives are normal: Não disse nada a ninguém. nunca , jamais , nada , ninguém reinforce negation Nunca como carne. · Não tenho nada. · Não conheço ninguém aqui. I never eat meat. · I have nothing. · I don't know anyone here. Related: Asking nicely · Tu vs você
lessonText.presente-irregular: Present tense — irregular verbs Irregular present A small set of ultra-common verbs break the regular patterns in the present. Learn these first — they appear in almost every conversation. Ser, estar, ir, ter, fazer, dar, ver, saber, querer, poder — present highlights. A2 presente-irregular Ser & estar eu tu ele/ela nós eles ser sou és é somos são estar estou estás está estamos estão Ir, ter, vir ir vou vais vai vamos vão ter tenho tens tem temos têm vir venho vens vem vimos vêm Fazer, dar, ver, saber fazer faço fazes faz fazemos fazem dar dou das dá damos dão ver vejo vês vê vemos veem saber sei sabes sabe sabemos sabem Querer & poder querer quero queres quer queremos querem poder posso podes pode podemos podem Vou ao mercado. · Tenho dois filhos. · Faço o jantar. · Sei nadar. · Quero um bica. · Podes ajudar-me? Don't memorise isolated endings — learn each verb in a short sentence. Check every form on the verb list . Related: Core verbs · Regular present · Ser vs estar
lessonText.adjectives: Adjectives Adjectives Portuguese adjectives agree in gender and number with the noun they describe. Position (before or after the noun) can change nuance. Agreement, position, and bom/bem vs mau/mal. A2 adjectives Gender and number agreement um carro novo · uma casa nova · carros novos · casas novas Adjective endings match the noun. After ser / estar (predicative) O café está quente. · Ela é inteligente. · Estamos cansados. Position: before vs after the noun Most descriptive adjectives come after the noun (um livro interessante). Some common ones often come before and may shift meaning: um grande homem (great man) vs um homem grande (big man) · uma velha amiga (old friend) vs uma amiga velha (elderly friend) Bom/bem and mau/mal Adjective (describes noun) Adverb (describes verb) bom / boa — good bem — well mau / má — bad mal — badly / poorly É um bom café. · Falas bem português. · Sinto-me mal. It's a good coffee. · You speak Portuguese well. · I feel unwell. Related: Ser vs estar · Adverbs · Articles & gender
lessonText.conjunctions: Conjunctions Conjunctions Conjunctions link words, phrases, or clauses. A handful of coordinators (e, mas, ou, porque) and subordinators (quando, se, que) cover most A2 writing and speech. E, mas, ou, porque, quando, se — overview. A2 conjunctions Coordinating — join equal parts Word Use Example e and Chá e café mas but Quero ir, mas estou cansado ou or Segunda ou terça? porque because Fico em casa porque chove portanto / por isso so / therefore Chove, por isso fico Subordinating — introduce a clause quando — when: Quando chegares, telefona. se — if: Se chover, ficamos em casa. (often triggers subjunctive later) que — that: Penso que ele vem. (indicative after many verbs) embora — although: Embora chova, vou sair. At B2 you'll meet more subordinators and the subjunctive after many of them — see Subjunctive overview . Related: Questions · Relative pronouns
lessonText.clitics-intro: Clitic pronouns — introduction Clitics (intro) Object pronouns (me, te, o, a, lhe…) usually attach to the verb in European Portuguese. In simple affirmative sentences they come after the verb — EP default is enclisis. Me, te, o, a — placement after the verb; EP proclisis with não. A2 clitics-intro Starter set Direct object Example me, te, o/a, nos, vos, os/as Ele vê- me . · Ajudo- te . · Compro- o . After the verb (affirmative) Diz-me a verdade. · Telefono-te amanhã. · Ela convida-nos. Hyphen in writing; pronounced as one unit. Before the verb (proclisis) Negative sentences and many “magnetic” words pull the pronoun before the verb: Não me digas isso. · Nunca te vi. · Quando me telefonas? Não, nunca, question words, subordinating conjunctions… A sentence cannot start with a clitic in standard EP — * Me ajuda is ungrammatical; say Ajuda-me or Podes ajudar-me? EP prefers proclisis more than Brazilian PT in some contexts, but affirmative declaratives still use enclisis: Ele disse-me . Related: Clitics (advanced) · Reflexive verbs · dizer
lessonText.past-future: Past & future — first steps Past & future Beyond the present, you'll soon need the pretérito perfeito (completed past), a taste of imperfeito (ongoing / background past), and ir + a + infinitive for near future in EP. Regular -ar past, key irregulars, imperfeito intro, ir+a+infinitive. A2 past-future Pretérito perfeito — regular -ar (falar) eu falei nós falámos tu falaste vocês falaram ele/ela falou eles/elas falaram Regular -er/-ir: comi, bebeu, partiu… Key irregulars in the perfeito ser/ir fui (same form!) ter tive estar estive fazer fiz dar dei ver vi vir vim Ontem fui ao cinema. · Tive uma ideia. · Fiz o jantar. Imperfeito — snapshot Background, habit, or ongoing past. Regular -ar: -ava endings (eu falava, tu falavas…). Used with perfeito for narratives: Quando era criança, ia muito à praia. · Estava a chover quando cheguei. When I was a child… · It was raining when I arrived. Near future: ir + a + infinitive (EP) Vou falar com ela amanhã. · Vamos jantar fora? Also common: simple present for near future (Amanhã vou ao médico). Practise: ir , fazer · Related: Compound tenses · Asking nicely (imperfeito for politeness)
lessonText.por-para: Por vs para Por vs para Por and para both translate many English “for / through / to” uses — but they split movement, beneficiary, duration, and exchange in predictable ways. Movement, beneficiary, duration, and common fixed phrases. B1 por-para Quick split para — destination, purpose, recipient (toward a goal) por — cause, duration, route, exchange rate, “on behalf of” Para — destination & purpose Vou para Lisboa. · Este presente é para ti. · Estudo para aprender. Going to Lisbon. · This gift is for you. · I study in order to learn. Por — duration, cause, route Fiquei por duas horas. · Obrigado pelo presente. · Passámos por Coimbra. I stayed for two hours. · Thanks for the gift. · We passed through Coimbra. Fixed phrases to learn por favor · por isso · por exemplo para sempre · para que (purpose) por telefone / por email — by phone / by email Some verbs take por idiomatically ( interessar-se por ). Learn those as chunks — see Preposition pairings . Related: Prepositions in depth · Preposition pairings
lessonText.prepositions-depth: Prepositions in depth Prepositions (depth) The core prepositions de, em, a, com drive location, origin, and direction. They merge with articles into contractions you'll use every day. De, em, a, com — contractions table and questions with prepositions. B1 prepositions-depth Core prepositions Prep. Typical sense Example de from, of Venho de Faro em in, at Estou em casa a to, at (movement/time) Vou a pé · Às três horas com with Vou contigo Contractions de + em + a + do, da, dos, das no, na, nos, nas ao, à, aos, às de + ele/ela/eles → dele, dela, deles, delas · em + ele… → nele, nela… Questions with prepositions In EP the preposition often stays at the end (or before the verb in formal style): De onde és? · Com quem vais? · Para onde vamos? Where are you from? · Who are you going with? · Where are we going? Related: Por vs para · Articles · Personal pronouns
lessonText.personal-pronouns: Personal pronouns Personal pronouns Subject pronouns (eu, tu, ele…) are often dropped when context is clear. Portuguese also has tonic pronouns (mim, ti, ele…) after prepositions and clitic unstressed forms attached to verbs. Eu, tu, ele — tonic vs clitic overview. B1 personal-pronouns Subject pronouns eu nós tu (informal EP) vocês ele / ela / você eles / elas Ele/ela/você share verb forms; so do eles/elas/vocês . Tonic pronouns (after prepositions) Isto é para mim. · Vou contigo. · Falo de ti. Not *para eu, *com tu — use mim, ti, ele, ela, nós, vocês. Clitic pronouns (objects) Unstressed forms attach to the verb (or come before it with não, etc.): Dá-me o livro. · Não me digas. · Ele viu-a ontem. Related: Clitics (intro) · Tu vs você · Reflexive
lessonText.reflexive: Reflexive verbs Reflexive verbs Many verbs add -se in the infinitive when the subject acts on themselves: lavar-se (to wash oneself). The reflexive pronoun (me, te, se…) matches the subject. -se verbs, lavar-se, reflexive pronouns. B1 reflexive Forms Eu lavo-me. · Tu levantas-te cedo. · Ela veste-se. · Nós sentamo-nos. Hyphen when enclitic; mesa alone in EP: sentamos-nos. Common reflexive verbs chamar-se — to be called · Como te chamas? sentir-se — to feel · Sinto-me bem. deitar-se — to lie down · Deito-me às onze. lembrar-se de — to remember esquecer-se de — to forget Some verbs are always reflexive in Portuguese but not in English ( queixar-se de — to complain). Learn them as phrases. Related: Clitics (intro) · Preposition pairings · chamar
lessonText.present-continuous: Present continuous (EP) Present continuous European Portuguese forms the present continuous with estar + a + infinitive — not the gerund (-ando/-endo) used in Brazil. Estar a + infinitive — the EP progressive. B1 present-continuous Pattern: conjugated estar + a + infinitive Estou a estudar português. · Ela está a cozinhar. · Estamos a ver um filme. I am studying Portuguese. · She is cooking. · We are watching a film. O que estás a fazer? · Estão a trabalhar em casa. Brazilian PT: estou estudando . In EP that sounds foreign — use estou a estudar . Related: Ser vs estar · Past continuous · estar
lessonText.past-continuous: Past continuous (EP) Past continuous Ongoing action in the past uses estar (imperfect) + a + infinitive in European Portuguese. Estava a + infinitive — past progressive in EP. B1 past-continuous Pattern: estava / estavas / estava… + a + infinitive Estava a chover quando chegaste. · Eles estavam a jantar. It was raining when you arrived. · They were having dinner. O que estavas a fazer ontem às oito? What were you doing yesterday at eight? Contrast with pretérito perfeito for a completed event: Estava a dormir quando o telefone tocou. Related: Present continuous · Past & future
lessonText.relative-pronouns: Relative pronouns Relative pronouns Relative pronouns introduce clauses that describe a noun: que (that/which/who), quem (who, for people), onde (where), cujo (whose). Que, quem, onde, cujo — brief overview. B1 relative-pronouns Que — general A mulher que telefonou. · O livro que li. · A cidade que visitámos. Works for people and things. Quem — people (often after preposition) A pessoa com quem falei. · Quem chegar primeiro, ganha. Onde — place A casa onde nasci. · O café onde nos encontrámos. Cujo — whose ( agrees with the possessed noun) O autor cujo livro ganhou o prémio. · A mulher cuja mala se perdeu. Cujo/cuja/cujos/cujas match the thing owned, not the owner. Related: Conjunctions · Questions
lessonText.quantity-determiners: Quantity & determiners Quantity determiners Words like muito, pouco, algum, nenhum, todo express amount or scope. They agree in gender and number when they modify a noun. Muito, pouco, algum, nenhum, todo. B1 quantity-determiners Word Sense Example muito/a/os/as much, many, very muita gente pouco/a little, few pouco tempo algum/a, uns/umas some alguns amigos nenhum/a none, not any Não tenho nenhuma ideia todo/a/os/as all, every, whole todo o dia cada each cada pessoa Há muita gente aqui. · Comi pouco. · Não vi ninguém. · Trabalho todo o dia. Muito before adjectives/adverbs is invariable: muito bom , muito bem . Related: Adjectives · Articles
lessonText.tu-vs-voce: Tu vs você Tu vs você European Portuguese favours tu in everyday speech among adults. Você is formal or careful; it uses third-person verb forms (você fala, not *você falas). EP prefers tu; você is formal with 3rd-person conjugation. B1 tu-vs-voce tu + 2nd person verb: Como estás? · Onde vives? você + 3rd person verb: Como está? · Onde vive? vocês + 3rd person plural: Como estão? When to use você in EP Formal service (some contexts): shops, official settings Addressing someone much older or in a clear hierarchy When you want distance or respect Informal: Onde estás? · Formal: Onde está o senhor? Possessives shift too: teu/tua with tu, seu/sua with você (same forms as “his/her” — context matters). Related: Personal pronouns · Imperative · Asking nicely
lessonText.adverbs: Adverbs Adverbs Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs — place, time, manner, degree. Many end in -mente (rapidamente); some are invariable (bem, mal, já, ainda). Place, time, manner, degree — bem/mal, já/ainda. B1 adverbs Manner (-mente / irregular) Fala claramente. · Corre rapidamente. · Fala bem português. · Canta mal. Place & time Place: aqui, aí, ali, cá, lá, dentro, fora Time: hoje, ontem, amanhã, cedo, tarde, sempre, nunca já — already / by now · ainda — still / yet Já comeste? · Ainda não. · Ainda estou a trabalhar. Have you eaten already? · Not yet. · I'm still working. Degree Muito bom. · Pouco interessante. · Demasiado caro. Related: Adjectives · Negation
lessonText.imperative: Imperative Imperative Commands and requests use the imperativo. Affirmative tu forms are often irregular; negative commands use the present subjunctive for all persons. Tu/você forms, negative imperatives with subjunctive. B2 imperative Affirmative — tu vs você Verb tu (informal) você / vocês (subjunctive forms) falar fala fale / falem comer come coma / comam ser sê seja / sejam estar está esteja / estejam Fala mais devagar! · Não fales assim! · Sentem-se, por favor. Affirmative tu vs negative tu (subjunctive). Negative imperative All persons use present subjunctive in negative commands: Não fumes. · Não fale. · Não comamos tarde. · Não se preocupem. Polite requests often avoid bare imperatives — use queria / podia or se faz favor . Related: Subjunctive · Tu vs você · ser
lessonText.conditional: Conditional Conditional The condicional (-ia endings) expresses hypothetical outcomes, polite requests, and “would” in English. EP also uses imperfeito for courtesy in speech. -ia endings, polite requests, conditional compound mention. B2 conditional Regular pattern (falar) eu falaria nós falaríamos tu falarías vocês falaríam ele/ela falaria eles/elas falaríam Uses Compraria uma casa se tivesse dinheiro. · Podia ajudar-me? (conditional or courtesy imperfeito) Hypothetical · Polite request. Condicional composto (brief) Teria + participle for unconfirmed past hypotheses: Teria perdido o comboio (I would have missed the train / I may have missed it). Related: Asking nicely · Subjunctive · Compound tenses
lessonText.subjunctive: Subjunctive (conjuntivo) Subjunctive The conjuntivo handles doubt, emotion, hypotheticals, and many subordinate clauses. European Portuguese uses it more than English — learn common triggers (que, se, quando, para que). Quando, se, que triggers — present/imperfect/future overview. B2 subjunctive Common triggers (often + que) Wish / emotion: Espero que… · É pena que… Doubt / denial: Não creio que… · Talvez… Hypothesis: Se tiver tempo… (future subjunctive) Time / purpose: Quando chegares… · Para que saibas… Present subjunctive (snapshot) Espero que ele venha. · É importante que estudem. · Quer que eu fale? Imperfect subjunctive Hypothetical present/future or polite past: Se fosse rico, viajaria. · Gostaria que me dissessem a verdade. Future subjunctive After se/quando for a future condition: Se vieres, avisa. · Quando chegar, telefona. Don't map English subjunctive 1:1 — focus on set phrases and triggers. Related: Imperative · Personal infinitive · Conjunctions
lessonText.compound-tenses: Compound tenses Compound tenses Compound tenses combine an auxiliary (ter or sometimes haver) with a past participle. The pretérito perfeito composto is especially common in EP for recent or continuing relevance. Ter/haver + participle, perfeito composto, futuro composto brief. B2 compound-tenses Structure: auxiliary (conjugated) + past participle (agrees in gender/number only with ter when direct object clitic precedes — advanced) Pretérito perfeito composto Tenho comido menos. · Tem chovido muito. · Havemos trabalhado o dia todo. Often “have been …-ing” or recent past with present relevance. Futuro composto (brief) Teremos acabado antes das oito. · Assim que tiveres chegado, avisa. Future perfect / action completed before another future point. Ter vs haver as auxiliary Ter is default for most verbs. Haver appears in formal or set patterns (há havido, têm havido). See haver page. Related: Participles · Haver · ter
lessonText.participles: Past participles Participles Past participles (-ado / -ido) form compound tenses with ter and can act as adjectives. A list of irregular participles is worth memorising. Regular -ado/-ido, irregular list, auxiliary ter. B2 participles Regular forms falar → falado · comer → comido · partir → partido Common irregulars abrir → aberto cover → coberto dizer → dito escrever → escrito fazer → feito pôr → posto romper → roto ver → visto vir → vindo morrer → morto As adjectives a porta está fechada · um livro escrito em português Related: Compound tenses · ter
lessonText.clitics-advanced: Clitic pronouns — advanced Clitics (advanced) Beyond me/te, EP uses 3rd-person clitics o, a, os, as (direct) and lhe(s) (indirect). Pronouns can merge (de-lo) and appear in mesoclisis with future/conditional. 3rd person o/a, mesoclisis mention, merging pronouns. B2 clitics-advanced Third-person direct objects Vi-o ontem. · Comprei-a na loja. · Conheço-os de vista. O/a/os/as replace specific nouns (must agree). Indirect: lhe / lhes Dei-lhe o livro. · Escrevi-lhes um email. Merging pronouns Dá-mo = dá-me + o (give it to me) · Vou dar-ta (I'll give it to you) Written with hyphen; order rules apply. Mesoclisis (future / conditional) Dar-te-ei a resposta. · Dir-lhe-íamos amanhã. Pronoun inside future/conditional form — formal; often avoided in speech. In speech, rephrase to avoid mesoclisis: Vou dar-te a resposta . Related: Clitics (intro) · Reflexive · Personal infinitive
lessonText.personal-infinitive: Personal infinitive Personal infinitive The infinitivo pessoal inflects for person — unique to Portuguese. It appears after prepositions and in certain subordinate clauses. Para ires, antes de falarmos — inflected infinitive. B2 personal-infinitive Add endings to the infinitive: falar → falar es (tu), falar mos (nós)… After prepositions Para ires à festa, precisas de bilhete. · Antes de falarmos, ouve isto. For you to go… · Before we talk… Same forms as future subjunctive (regular verbs) For regular verbs, personal infinitive endings match future subjunctive — context tells them apart. É melhor ires agora. · Quando eles chegarem, começamos. Related: Subjunctive · Prepositions
lessonText.verb-contrasts: Verb contrasts Verb contrasts Several high-frequency verbs overlap in English but split in Portuguese. These contrasts unlock more natural EP. Ficar vs ser/estar, dizer/falar/contar, poder/conseguir. B2 verb-contrasts Ficar vs ser / estar ficar — stay, remain, become: Fico em casa. · Ficaste morena. ser — permanent trait · estar — temporary state Ficar often marks change: Fiquei surpreendido. Dizer vs falar vs contar dizer — say (specific words): Disse que sim. falar — speak / talk: Falo português. · Falar de / com contar — tell (a story), count: Conta-me tudo. Poder vs conseguir Não posso fumar aqui. (not allowed) · Não consigo abrir a janela. (can't manage physically) Poder = permission/possibility · Conseguir = manage to / succeed. Related: Ser vs estar · Preposition pairings · ficar , conseguir
